newsitem.title: UK: Bardon, Camas say trading as expected.
newsitem.headline: Bardon, Camas say trading as expected.

text.p: Bardon Group Plc and Camas Plc said on Monday that the current year had started as expected for both companies.
They also said their planned merger into Aggregate Industries would benefit from low relative tax rates.

The groups said that Bardon's UK and U.S. tax position, especially with regard to written off advance corporation tax (ACT), meant that the new group would benefit from a tax rate estimated at half the standard tax rate on medium-term profits.
The companies said the improvement in the UK housing market seen in the last quarter of 1996 had continued into 1997.
"Markets in the U.S. have enjoyed a period of sustained growth and all indications are that this is continuing in 1997," they said in a statement.

Bardon and Camas are of comparabale size, with Camas slightly the larger in terms of market capitalisation. Combined, the group's shareholder funds as at the end of 1996 would have been 561 million stg.

Combined output in 1996 would have been 40.6 million tonnes of dry stone, 7.4 million tonnes of coated stone, 2.6 million cubic metres of ready mix concrete and 3.4 million tonnes of pre-cast concrete products.
In the UK, Aggregate Industries will be the fifth largest aggregates producer and will be a leading operator in what remains a highly fragmented U.S. industry.
Bardon shares rose on news of the merger, touching 48 pence before settling for a three pence gain at 44-1/2. Camas shares were up eight at 92 pence after touching 93.
